description: Each budget sits at the measured decoded transfer for that page with about ten percent headroom, capped at the level this branch set, because the payload is dominated by the shared token stylesheet, the two self-hosted variable fonts and the status fetch rather than by page-specific weight. Mechanics: 'bytes' is the decoded payload of every response a page load causes and 'requests' counts those responses; both are deterministic and both are enforced. Every body is read and the page is left to settle before the total is taken, so a fast laptop and a shared runner report the same number. The decoded total includes the two self-hosted variable fonts (about 53 KB) and the design token stylesheet (about 60 KB), which compress far smaller on the wire. 'longTasks' is the number of main-thread tasks over 50 ms during the load and a short settle window, enforced where the engine reports them. The longest single block is measured and printed so a failure shows it, but it is not enforced: on a shared two-core runner the home page has reported anything from 17 ms to 2.6 s in the first frame, which is the runner's startup and not this site.
